question: During fermentation in yeast, pyruvate is converted into which of the following products?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethanol and carbon dioxide**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ethanol is a renewable **biofuel** primarily produced from crops like corn and sugarcane.
 
• When ethanol burns, it primarily produces** carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water,** making it a cleaner alternative to fossil fuels, although it still contributes to CO₂ emissions.
 
• Ethanol has the potential to be carbon-neutral if the CO₂ released during its combustion is offset by the CO₂ absorbed by the plants grown to produce it.
 
• **CO₂ is a byproduct **of ethanol fermentation, which can be captured for industrial use. 
 
• The use of ethanol in fuels can help reduce greenhouse gas emissions compared to conventional petroleum-based fuels, contributing to the fight against climate change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glucose and carbon dioxide**

 
 
• Glucose is a** primary energy source** for cells, broken down during cellular respiration.
 
• Carbon dioxide is produced as a byproduct when glucose is metabolized in the body.
 
• In **photosynthesis**, plants use carbon dioxide and convert it into glucose and oxygen.
 
• Glucose breakdown releases CO₂ during aerobic respiration, contributing to the **carbon cycle.**
 
 
 
• **Lactic acid and carbon dioxide**
 
 
• actic acid is produced during anaerobic respiration when **oxygen levels are low,** especially in muscles.
 
• Lactic acid buildup can cause **muscle fatigue **and soreness during intense exercise.
 
• Carbon dioxide is not produced in lactic acid fermentation; it's primarily a byproduct of aerobic respiration.
 
• Carbon dioxide is still released from the body through breathing, even when anaerobic respiration occurs.
 
 
 
• **Water and carbon dioxide**
 
 
• Water and carbon dioxide are the main byproducts of cellular respiration in living organisms.
 
• **Plants use CO₂ and water **in photosynthesis to produce glucose and oxygen.
 
• Water vapor and CO₂ are both key greenhouse gases, affecting Earth's climate.
 
• In combustion, fuels burn to produce water and carbon dioxide as waste products.
